decisions.choice: Qoheleth: one who gathers people and speaks to them; the speaker's title, used as a name
decisions.reason: The word (qohelet) comes from the root of qahal, "assembly", and means one who gathers an assembly or speaks to it. It is a feminine form of the kind used for an office, though the speaker is a man (1:12). It names him by what he does: he gathered people, and gathered and taught sayings (12:9-10). It occurs only in this book (1:1, 2, 12; 7:27; 12:8, 9, 10), mostly without "the", as a name, but once with it (12:8), as a title. Older Bibles call him "the Preacher"; others say "the Speaker".

decisions.choice: son of David, king in Jerusalem: the speaker is presented as a king of David's line; the book never names Solomon
alternatives: a later writer speaking in a royal persona
decisions.reason: Of David's sons only Solomon reigned over Israel in Jerusalem (1:12), and the speaker's wisdom, building and wealth in chapter 2 recall the account of Solomon in 1 Kings 3-10. But the book never gives his name, and "son" can mean any descendant. Readers differ: some take the voice to be Solomon's own, others a persona, a speaker who takes on Solomon's place in order to test where wisdom, pleasure and wealth lead. The translation keeps the book's own words and adds no name.

decisions.choice: the words of: a title for the whole book, spoken about Qoheleth from outside
decisions.reason: Books of prophets and sages open the same way (Jeremiah 1:1; Amos 1:1; Proverbs 30:1). Verses 1-2 speak of Qoheleth in the third person, as 12:8-14 do at the end; between them he speaks for himself. Neither voice takes quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the Teacher
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Qoheleth as a name. Balanced and Readable say what he does (m1), and "the Teacher" fits the end of the book, where he "taught the people knowledge" (12:9). The capital shows that it is the title the book calls him by. This wording holds through the book.

decisions.choice: "Qohélet" (L); "o Mestre" (B, R)

As the English: Literal keeps the Hebrew title as a name, spelled as Portuguese reads its sounds; Balanced and Readable say what he does (m1), and "o Mestre" fits 12:9, where he "taught the people". "o Pregador", the title of the older Portuguese Bibles, suggests a preacher in church. The capital marks the title the book calls him by.

decisions.choice: "ቆሔሌት" (L); "መምህሩ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the Hebrew title as a name, "ቆሔሌት"; Balanced and Readable say what he does, "መምህሩ" (the Teacher), which fits 12:9, where he taught the people knowledge. "ሰባኪው" would make him a preacher of sermons. This wording holds through the book.

decisions.choice: "कोहेलेत" (Literal); "उपदेशक" (Balanced, Readable) for Qoheleth
decisions.reason: Qoheleth is the speaker's title, used as a name; it comes from the word for gathering an assembly, so it names one who gathers people and speaks to them (m1). Literal keeps it as a name in Devanagari, "कोहेलेत", as the English Literal keeps "Qoheleth". Balanced and Readable say what he does, as the English "the Teacher" does: "उपदेशक" is one who teaches and counsels people, which fits the gathered hearers of the Hebrew word and 12:9, where he taught the people knowledge. "सभोपदेशक", the familiar name of the book in older Hindi Bibles, is not used, so that this translation's wording stays its own; "गुरु" is kept for "Rabbi, Teacher" in the New Testament, and "प्रचारक" would suggest a church preacher. The same forms stand wherever he is named (1:2, 1:12, 7:27, 12:8-10). Qoheleth is spoken of with plain third-person forms (वह, कहता है), as the speaker of a book, while God keeps the honorific (वे).

decisions.choice: "ये ... के वचन हैं"
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable make the title a sentence; Readable gives his family and office a sentence of their own. Literal brackets the words Hindi needs to join the titles to the name.

decisions.choice: Когелет (L); Учитель (B, R)
decisions.reason: Qoheleth is the speaker's title, one who gathers people and speaks to them, used as a name (m1). Literal keeps it as a name, transliterated from the Hebrew as Когелет, the form modern Russian scholarship uses, rather than the Greek Екклесиаст of the Synodal tradition, which reads as a book title. Balanced and Readable say what he does, as the English does with "the Teacher": Учитель fits 12:9, where he taught the people knowledge. Проповедник would suggest a church sermon, and Собиратель names the root rather than the office. The same three forms are kept through the book.

decisions.choice: Это слова
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the title a sentence, as the English does; Readable gives his family and office in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Qoheleth: "コヘレト" (L), the Hebrew title kept as a name; "教師" (B, R), "the Teacher", in every place it occurs (1:1, 1:2, 1:12, 7:27, 12:8-10)
alternatives: コヘレト at every level
decisions.reason: m1: one who gathers people and speaks to them, a title used as a name. Literal transliterates it as names are (コヘレト is simply the Hebrew sound, not a translation's wording). Balanced and Readable say what he does, as the English does with "the Teacher": 伝道者 suggests a Christian evangelist and is the choice of two copyrighted Bibles, and 集会で語る者 is too heavy to repeat as a name. 教師 also fits 12:9, where he "taught the people knowledge".

decisions.choice: Plain style (だ・である体) at every level, Readable too, for the whole book: the narrator's frame and Qoheleth's own reflections
alternatives: です・ます at Readable, as in the narrative books
decisions.reason: Ecclesiastes is a sage reflecting aloud, in prose and verse, not addressing an audience politely; the OT poetry rule and Proverbs and Job keep the plain voice at every level. God is spoken of with light respect forms (与えられた, なさる), never 彼. Commands to the reader (5:1, 11:9) are 〜せよ (L), 〜しなさい (B, R), as the father in Proverbs.

decisions.choice: "Когелет" as a name (L), "Учитель" (B, R), through the whole book
decisions.reason: The terms note keeps the Hebrew title as a name at Literal, transcribed with г for h, and says "the Teacher" at Balanced and Readable. "Екклезіаст" is the Greek title of the book and "Проповідник" suggests a church preacher; the meaning decision names the alternatives.

decisions.choice: breath: a breath or vapor, something real but brief that cannot be grasped; by extension what is passing, beyond understanding, or without lasting result
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) means a breath or a puff of vapor, the breath that shows in cold air and is gone (Psalm 39:6; 144:4; Job 7:16; Isaiah 57:13). It is the key word of this book, used about 38 times, from this verse to 12:8. It is also the name of Abel (Genesis 4:2), whose life was cut short. The picture carries several senses, and the book uses each of them: what is brief and soon gone (6:12; 11:10), what cannot be grasped or made sense of (8:14), and what comes to nothing, leaving no lasting result (2:11; 4:4). Some readers hear also the absurd: things that ought not to be so. The traditional "vanity" (from the Latin for "emptiness") and the modern "meaningless" each choose one of these senses. "Breath" keeps the picture, so that "everything is breath" can carry each sense where the context points to it. Later verses note where the sense leans one way.

decisions.choice: breath of breaths: the utmost breath, breath through and through
decisions.reason: Hebrew puts a noun before its own plural to say the highest degree, as in "the Song of Songs" (Song 1:1) and "the holy of holies" (Exodus 26:33). Said twice and then summed up, "everything is breath", the cry is as strong as the language can make it.

decisions.choice: says Qoheleth: the frame speaks about him, and the same words close the book
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for completed action, "said", used here to introduce a saying that holds good, as in "thus says". The same cry, "breath of breaths, says Qoheleth; everything is breath", stands at 12:8, so that it encloses all that Qoheleth says between.

decisions.choice: everything is breath: the book's tensions belong to the book
alternatives: reading the sayings so that they agree
decisions.reason: The book tests this claim against wisdom, pleasure, work, justice and death, and it sets sayings side by side that seem to pull against each other. Wisdom is better than folly, yet the wise die like fools (2:13-16). Toil is breath, yet eating, drinking and enjoying one's work are a gift from the hand of God (2:24). Sorrow is better than laughter (7:3), yet one is to eat bread with joy (9:7). The translation does not smooth these tensions away or choose between the sayings; they are part of what the book says, and its last words (12:13-14) are its own.

decisions.choice: Breath of breaths (L); Breath upon breath (B)
decisions.reason: Literal shows the Hebrew form (m2). Balanced keeps the picture and piles breath on breath, as the Hebrew does, in a form English can say. Both keep "breath" so that its range is left open (m1); the founder's ruling for the book does not use "meaningless". The same words return at 12:8.

decisions.choice: Nothing lasts! ... Everything passes like a breath.
decisions.reason: As the founder ruled for 1:2 and 12:8, Readable says what passes like a breath and keeps the picture. "Nothing lasts!" is said twice, for the doubled cry. Elsewhere Readable keeps the breath picture with the sense the context needs: "like a breath", "does not last" or "cannot be grasped".

decisions.choice: says
decisions.reason: English introduces a saying that still stands with "says" (m3).

decisions.choice: "soplo" (L, B); "Nada dura ... Todo pasa como un soplo" (R)
decisions.reason: Hevel is a breath (m1), and "soplo" keeps the picture, as Psalm 144:4 does, so that the word can carry each of its senses through the book: brief, beyond grasp, without result. Literal shows the Hebrew superlative ("Soplo de soplos"), Balanced piles breath on breath. "vanidad" (the traditional word) now says pride or emptiness and is not used. Readable says elsewhere "como un soplo", "no dura" or "no se puede atrapar", as the sense needs. The same cry returns at 12:8.

decisions.choice: « souffle » (L, B); « Rien ne dure ... Tout passe comme un souffle » (R)
decisions.reason: Hevel is a breath (m1); « souffle » keeps the picture, as Psalm 144:4 does, so the word can carry each of its senses through the book: brief, beyond grasp, without result. Literal shows the Hebrew superlative (« Souffle des souffles »), Balanced piles breath on breath. « vanité », the traditional word, now says conceit and is not used. Readable says elsewhere « comme un souffle », « ne dure pas » or « insaisissable », as the sense needs. The same cry returns at 12:8.

decisions.choice: "pumzi" (L, B); "Hakuna kinachodumu ... kama pumzi" (R)
decisions.reason: Hevel is a breath (m1); "pumzi" keeps the picture, as Psalm 144:4 does, so the word can carry each of its senses through the book: brief, beyond grasp, without result. "ubatili" (futility, the familiar word) names only one of them. Because "pumzi" stands for hevel in this book, life-breath (ruach) is "roho". Readable says elsewhere "kama pumzi", "haidumu" or "haishikiki", as the sense needs. The same cry returns at 12:8.

decisions.choice: "hơi thở" (L, B); "Chẳng có gì tồn tại ... như một hơi thở" (R)
decisions.reason: Hevel is a breath (m1); "hơi thở" keeps the picture, as Psalm 144:4 and Proverbs 31:30 do, so the word can carry each of its senses through the book: brief, beyond grasp, without result. "hư không" (emptiness), the wording of the 1925 version, names only one of them. Because "hơi thở" stands for hevel here, life-breath (ruach) is "sinh khí" in this book. Readable says elsewhere "như một hơi thở", "chẳng tồn tại lâu" or "không nắm bắt được", as the sense needs.

decisions.choice: "입김" (L, B); "아무것도 남지 않는다 ... 입김처럼 지나간다" (R)
decisions.reason: Hevel is a breath (m1); "입김", the breath that shows in cold air, keeps the picture, as Proverbs 31:30 and Psalm 144:4 do, so the word can carry each of its senses through the book: brief, beyond grasp, without result. "헛되다", the familiar word of the Korean Bibles, names only one of them. Readable says elsewhere "입김 같다", "오래가지 않는다" or "붙잡을 수 없다", as the sense needs. The same cry returns at 12:8.

decisions.choice: "sopro" (L, B); "Nada dura! ... Tudo passa como um sopro" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book. Hevel is a breath (m1), and "sopro" keeps the picture, as Psalms 39 and 62 do in Portuguese, so that the one word can carry each of its senses through the book: brief, beyond grasp, without result. "Vaidade" (the older Bibles' word) now means conceit, and "inútil" or "passageiro" would each choose one sense. Literal shows the Hebrew superlative ("Sopro de sopros"); Balanced piles breath on breath. Readable says elsewhere "como um sopro", "não dura" or "não se pode agarrar", as the sense needs. The same cry returns at 12:8. Because "sopro" stands for hevel in this book, ruach is "vento" (wind) or "espírito" (the life-breath, 3:19), never "sopro".

decisions.choice: "እስትንፋስ" (L, B); "ምንም አይዘልቅም" and "እንደ እስትንፋስ" (R); "breath of breaths" "የእስትንፋስ እስትንፋስ" (L), "እስትንፋስ፣ ፍጹም እስትንፋስ" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads hevel as breath: real but brief and beyond grasping, not worthless. "እስትንፋስ" says that and is the word used for hevel in Psalms 39 and 62; "ከንቱ" would say the world is empty or useless. Literal keeps the Hebrew superlative as a genitive; Balanced makes it "breath, utter breath". Readable follows the English Readable ("like a breath", "nothing lasts"): "እንደ እስትንፋስ" and "ምንም አይዘልቅም". The same wording holds for every hevel in the book, and 12:8 repeats this verse.

decisions.choice: Romans 8:20 echo: the Hebrew is followed
decisions.reason: Romans 8:20 says creation was subjected to "ከንቱነት" (futility), the Greek word the Septuagint uses for hevel here. Paul does not quote the verse, so the Amharic keeps "እስትንፋስ" from the Hebrew and its meaning decision.

decisions.choice: "साँस" for hevel; the motto is "साँसों की साँस" (Literal), "साँस पर साँस" (Balanced), "कुछ भी नहीं टिकता! ... साँस की तरह बीत जाता है" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Hevel is a breath or vapor, something real but brief that no one can grasp (m1). The English keeps the picture at every level, and so does the Hindi, with "साँस", the word the Psalms in this translation use for hevel (39:5-6, 11; 144:4). Literal "साँसों की साँस" shows the Hebrew way of saying the utmost degree (m2), as "गीतों का गीत" does. Balanced piles breath on breath, as the English does. Readable, as the founder ruled for the English at 1:2 and 12:8, cries "nothing lasts" twice and keeps the picture in "साँस की तरह बीत जाता है". The older Hindi word "व्यर्थ" (vain, useless) chooses only one of the senses; where the English Readable spells a sense out ("that does not last", "that makes no sense"), the Hindi Readable does too. The motto has this wording at each level here and at 12:8.

decisions.choice: "कहता है"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "said" introduces a saying that still stands (m3); Hindi, like the English, uses the present.

decisions.choice: дуновение дуновений (L); дуновение за дуновением ... лишь дуновение (B); Всё мимолётно! ... как лёгкое дыхание (R)
decisions.reason: Hevel is a breath or vapor, real but brief and impossible to grasp (m1). Literal and Balanced keep the picture with дуновение, the word the Russian Psalms already use for hevel (39:6; 62:10), so that "всё — дуновение" can carry each of its senses; Literal shows the Hebrew superlative, Balanced piles breath on breath. Readable says what passes and keeps the picture with как лёгкое дыхание, the Readable form of the Psalms. The Synodal's суета сует is not used at any level: in modern Russian суета means fuss and bustle, which is not the Hebrew picture. Through the book hevel is дуновение (L), лишь дуновение (B), and at Readable как лёгкое дыхание, мимолётно or a phrase for the sense the verse needs.

decisions.choice: говорит, set off with dashes, no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The frame speaks about Qoheleth (m3) and, as in the English, takes no quotation marks; Russian sets the inserted "says" off with dashes. The same words close the book (12:8).

decisions.choice: hevel: "息" with one form per level through the book: the refrain "息の中の息" (L), "息また息" (B), "何も残らない" (R); "everything is breath" "すべては息である" (L), "すべては息にすぎない" (B), "すべては息のように消えていく" (R); "this too is breath" "これもまた息である" (L), "これもまた息にすぎない" (B), "これもまた息のようなものだ" (R)
decisions.reason: m1: a breath or vapor, real but brief and beyond grasping. 空 (emptiness) is the word Japanese readers know from older Bibles, but it says only one of the senses and loses the image; 息 keeps it, as the English does. 息の中の息 follows the Hebrew superlative as 歌の中の歌 does; 息また息 piles the word up as "breath upon breath" does (cf. 山また山). Readable follows the English R.

decisions.choice: "подих" for hevel at Literal and Balanced, through the book; "Подих подихів" (L), "Подих над подихами" (B), "Ніщо не триває! Усе минає, як подих" (R) at 1:2 and 12:8

The familiar "марнота" and "суєта" decide for futility. "Над" in Balanced gives the superlative, as in "Пісня над піснями"; Readable follows the founder's ruling for 1:2.

alternatives: commas, as at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Readable's exclamations end in "!", and Ukrainian sets an interrupting "says" after an exclamation off with dashes. The words are not marked as a quotation, as in the English.

decisions.choice: gain: what is left over, a lasting profit
decisions.reason: The word (yitron) is found only in this book, ten times (1:3; 2:11, 13; 3:9; 5:8, 15; 7:12; 10:10, 11). It comes from a root meaning to remain or be left over, and it is a word of accounts: what is left when everything has been added up. The question is not whether work achieves anything at all, but whether anything remains to a person in the end. Qoheleth gives his answer in 2:11: "there was no gain under the sun".

decisions.choice: toil: hard, wearing work, and what it earns
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb ('amal) mean work that wears a person out; elsewhere the noun means trouble or misery (Job 5:7; Psalm 90:10). In this book they cover both the effort and what it earns, the wealth a person leaves behind (2:18-19). They are among the book's key words. "His toil which he toils" doubles the word for weight.

decisions.choice: under the sun: in this world, in human life as it can be seen from the earth
decisions.reason: The phrase (tachat hashemesh) occurs 29 times in this book and nowhere else in the Bible. It marks out the field of Qoheleth's search: life as a person on earth can see and test it, where the sun rises and sets (1:5). "Under the heavens" (1:13; 2:3; 3:1) means the same. It does not mean the world without God; God is at work in it throughout the book (1:13; 2:24-26; 3:10-14).

decisions.choice: what gain is there: a question that expects the answer "none"
decisions.reason: The question opens Qoheleth's search, and the poem that follows (verses 4-11) gives its first answer: the earth, the sun, the wind and the streams go round and round, and nothing is added.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: people ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word ('adam) means any human being. Balanced and Readable speak of people in general, which needs no setting; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

decisions.choice: gain ... hard work (B); what good ... hard work (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled words: yitron is "gain" at Literal and Balanced and "what good it does" at Readable; 'amal is "toil" at Literal and "hard work" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: here on earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means (m3). Literal and Balanced keep "under the sun", which the book repeats as a refrain. Readable says "here on earth" or "in this world" wherever it stands.

decisions.choice: "bajo el sol" (L, B); "aquí en la tierra", "en este mundo" (R)
decisions.reason: The book's refrain (m3) stays word for word at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it means wherever it stands.

decisions.choice: "ganancia" (L, B), "de qué sirve" (R); "afán" (L), "duro trabajo" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled words for yitron and 'amal, kept the same through the book. "afán" keeps at Literal the doubled noun and verb of the Hebrew ("su afán con que se afana").

decisions.choice: {{gender:la persona|el hombre}} for "a person"; {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} for humankind; {{gender:los hijos de la humanidad|los hijos de los hombres}} for the sons of humankind (1:13); no span on "su", "lo", "le" or the verbs
alternatives: spans on the possessives and pronouns
decisions.reason: Spanish has two wordings only in the noun, so the gender setting stands on the noun, with the article, preposition, determiner or adjective that agrees with it inside the span ({{gender:del ser humano|del hombre}}, {{gender:toda persona|todo hombre}}, {{gender:persona justa|hombre justo}}). "su", "lo", "le" and the verbs read the same for a man or a woman, so where the English spans "their / his" or "they / he" Spanish has nothing to change. Where a pronoun must refer back to the person, Spanish uses "el ser humano", masculine in both options, or rephrases (6:12). This holds through the book.

decisions.choice: « sous le soleil » (L, B); « ici-bas », « dans ce monde » (R)
decisions.reason: The book's refrain (m3) stays word for word at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it means wherever it stands.

decisions.choice: « gain » (L, B), « à quoi sert » (R); « peine » (L), « dur travail » (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled words for yitron and 'amal. French has no verb « peiner » that takes the noun as object, so Literal repeats the noun (« sa peine, la peine qu'il se donne ») to keep the Hebrew doubling.

decisions.choice: {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} (also un / tout / d’être humain); {{gender:enfants des humains|fils des hommes}} for the sons of humankind (1:13); no span on « son », « sa », « ses », « il », « le » or « on »
decisions.reason: French puts the gender setting on nouns only, with an agreeing article or adjective inside the span when it differs between the options; possessives and pronouns take none, since the generic « il » and « on » already speak of anyone, as the French style guide sets. For the sons of humankind the published form of the Psalms and Proverbs is used; « fils de l’homme » would read as the title Son of Man. This holds through the book.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "ሰው", "ሰዎች" and "የሰው ልጆች"
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "a person"/"a man" as a gender setting. Amharic "ሰው" (and "የሰው ልጆች" for the sons of humankind) already means a human being of either sex, and the masculine verb is the generic form, so Amharic has only one wording and no span. decisions.choice: "ትርፍ" (gain); "ድካም" (toil); "ከፀሐይ በታች" (under the sun)
decisions.reason: The book's key words keep one Amharic word each through all twelve chapters: yitron "ትርፍ" (what is left over, a profit), ʿamal "ድካም" with the verb "ደከመ" (wearing work), and "ከፀሐይ በታች" at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "በዚህ ምድር ላይ" or "በዚህ ዓለም" where the English Readable says "here on earth" or "in this world".

decisions.choice: "सूर्य के नीचे" at every level; "आकाश के नीचे" for "under the heavens"
decisions.reason: "Under the sun" (m3) is the book's refrain, meaning life in this world as it is seen from the earth. The English Readable says "here on earth" or "in this world"; the Hindi keeps "सूर्य के नीचे" at every level, as the poetry note settles, since the plain Hindi phrase is understood as life in this world and its repetition holds the book together. "Under the heavens" (1:13; 2:3; 3:1), which means the same, is "आकाश के नीचे" at every level.

decisions.choice: yitron: "लाभ" (Literal, Balanced), "क्या भला होता है" (Readable); 'amal: "परिश्रम" (Literal), "कड़ी मेहनत" or "मेहनत" (Balanced), "मेहनत" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's settled words, following the English levels (r-en-3): yitron is a lasting profit (m1), 'amal is hard, wearing work and what it earns (m2). The same Hindi words are kept for them through the book.

decisions.choice: no gender span on "मनुष्य", "वह", "उसके"
decisions.reason: Hindi "मनुष्य" means any human being, and the generic masculine verb (करता है) is ordinary Hindi for anyone, so the gender setting has nothing to change here. Through the book the Hindi has no span on these words where the English has one; only "children of humankind / sons of men" keeps the span the Psalms use, "{{gender:मनुष्य की सन्तान|मनुष्य के पुत्रों}}".

decisions.choice: под солнцем
decisions.reason: The book's refrain (m3) is под солнцем at every level, Readable included, where the English Readable says "here on earth": the phrase is plain in Russian, means life in this world, and keeps the refrain audible at every level.

decisions.choice: выгода (L, B), толк (R); труд (L), тяжкий труд (B), тяжёлая работа (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled words: yitron, a lasting gain or profit (m1), is выгода at Literal and Balanced and какой толк at Readable; 'amal, hard and wearing work (m2), is труд at Literal, тяжкий труд at Balanced and тяжёлая работа at Readable, throughout the book.

decisions.choice: человек ... он, no gender span
decisions.reason: Russian человек means any human being, man or woman, and its pronoun он follows the noun's grammar, so Russian has no second wording where the English Literal has a gender span for "a person / a man" and its pronouns. This holds for the whole chapter; children of humankind (1:13) keeps the span the Psalms use.

decisions.choice: "under the sun": "太陽の下で" (L, B) throughout; Readable as the English R: "この地上で" for "here on earth", "この世で" for "in this world"
alternatives: この世で at every level
decisions.reason: 太陽の下 keeps the book's own phrase and is plain modern Japanese; 日の下 is the older Bible form. Readable says what it means (m3: human life as seen from the earth), as the English R does.

decisions.choice: yitron "gain": "益" (L, B), Readable by sense ("何の役に立つのか", "何が残るのか"); amal "toil": "労苦" (L, B), "苦労" / "一生懸命に働く" (R)
decisions.reason: m1: what is left over, a lasting profit; 益 is the lasting benefit, where 利益 sounds commercial. 労苦 is hard, wearing work (m2). These forms hold through the book.

decisions.choice: no gender span where the English has one for "a person ... their": "людина" and its feminine pronouns are already inclusive
decisions.reason: The style guide gives no gender span where Ukrainian is already inclusive ("людина", "люди", "кожен", "хто"). The Hebrew word means a human being, which "людина" says. For the whole book, spans stay only where Ukrainian has two real wordings, such as "діти людські" and "сини людські".

decisions.choice: "здобуток" (L), "що здобувають" (B), "яка користь" (R) for yitron; "труд" (L), "тяжка праця" (B, R) for amal; "під сонцем" (L, B), "тут, на землі" or "у цьому світі" (R), through the book
decisions.reason: The terms note's rows for the book: gain, toil and under the sun, with Readable saying what they mean. "Труд" and "трудитися" keep the Hebrew repetition at Literal.

source.text: דּ֤וֹר הֹלֵךְ֙ וְד֣וֹר בָּ֔א וְהָאָ֖רֶץ לְעוֹלָ֥ם עֹמָֽדֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: A generation [is] going, and a generation [is] coming, and the earth forever [is] standing.

en.L: A generation goes and a generation comes, \q and the earth stands forever.
en.B: One generation goes and another comes, \q but the earth remains forever.
en.R: One generation passes away and another one comes, \q but the earth is always there.

es.L: Una generación va y una generación viene, \q y la tierra permanece para siempre.
es.B: Una generación se va y otra llega, \q pero la tierra permanece para siempre.
es.R: Una generación pasa y viene otra, \q pero la tierra sigue siempre ahí.

fr.L: Une génération s’en va et une génération vient, \q et la terre demeure pour toujours.
fr.B: Une génération s’en va, une autre arrive, \q mais la terre subsiste à jamais.
fr.R: Une génération disparaît, une autre arrive, \q mais la terre est toujours là.

sw.L: Kizazi kinakwenda na kizazi kinakuja, \q na dunia inasimama milele.
sw.B: Kizazi kimoja kinapita na kingine kinakuja, \q lakini dunia inadumu milele.
sw.R: Kizazi kimoja kinatoweka na kingine kinakuja, \q lakini dunia ipo pale pale daima.

vi.L: Một thế hệ đi và một thế hệ đến, \q và đất đứng vững mãi mãi.
vi.B: Thế hệ này qua đi, thế hệ khác đến, \q nhưng trái đất vẫn còn mãi.
vi.R: Thế hệ này qua đời, thế hệ khác đến, \q nhưng trái đất thì lúc nào cũng còn đó.

ko.L: 한 세대가 가고 한 세대가 오며, \q 땅은 영원히 서 있다.
ko.B: 한 세대가 가면 또 한 세대가 오지만, \q 땅은 영원히 그대로 있다.
ko.R: 한 세대가 세상을 떠나면 다른 세대가 오지만, \q 땅은 언제나 그 자리에 있다.

pt.L: Uma geração se vai e uma geração vem, \q e a terra fica de pé para sempre.
pt.B: Uma geração se vai e outra chega, \q mas a terra continua para sempre.
pt.R: Uma geração morre e outra nasce, \q mas a terra está sempre ali.

am.L: ትውልድ ይሄዳል፤ ትውልድም ይመጣል፤ \q ምድርም ለዘላለም ትቆማለች።
am.B: አንድ ትውልድ ያልፋል፤ ሌላውም ይመጣል፤ \q ምድር ግን ለዘላለም ትኖራለች።
am.R: አንዱ ትውልድ ያልፋል፤ ሌላውም ይመጣል። \q ምድር ግን ሁልጊዜ አለች።

hi.L: एक पीढ़ी जाती है और एक पीढ़ी आती है, \q और पृथ्वी सदा खड़ी रहती है।
hi.B: एक पीढ़ी जाती है और दूसरी आती है, \q पर पृथ्वी सदा बनी रहती है।
hi.R: एक पीढ़ी मरकर चली जाती है और दूसरी आ जाती है, \q पर धरती हमेशा वहीं रहती है।

ru.L: Поколение уходит, и поколение приходит, \q и земля вечно стоит.
ru.B: Одно поколение уходит, другое приходит, \q а земля остаётся навсегда.
ru.R: Одно поколение умирает, и приходит другое, \q а земля всегда остаётся на месте.

ja.L: 世代が行き、世代が来る、 \q そして地はとこしえに立っている。
ja.B: 一つの世代が去り、次の世代が来る。 \q しかし、地はいつまでも変わらずにある。
ja.R: 一つの世代が過ぎ去り、また次の世代がやって来る。 \q けれども、大地はいつまでもそこにある。

uk.L: Покоління відходить, і покоління приходить, \q а земля навіки стоїть.
uk.B: Одне покоління відходить, і приходить інше, \q а земля стоїть навіки.
uk.R: Одне покоління минає, і приходить інше, \q а земля завжди залишається.

decisions.choice: verses 4-11: a poem
decisions.reason: The passage is built from short, balanced lines that answer each other, and it is set in lines. Most of the rest of the book is reflective prose; the next poem is 3:1-8.

decisions.choice: goes ... comes: one generation dies and another is born
decisions.reason: "Go" is used of dying (Psalm 39:14; Job 10:21). The order, going before coming, puts the endless passing first.

decisions.choice: generation: the people living at one time
decisions.reason: The word (dor) is a generation of people (Exodus 1:6). Generations pass the way the sun, the wind and the streams pass in the next verses.

decisions.choice: the earth stands forever: it remains, while people pass
decisions.reason: The earth outlasts each generation, but it does not move on; it stays where it is, as the sun, wind and streams go round and come back. Lasting brings people no gain. The word for "forever" ('olam) is the one used in 3:11.

decisions.choice: but
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the lines with "and", which here sets the lasting earth against the passing generations. Literal keeps "and".

decisions.choice: passes away ... is always there
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that "goes" means to die (m2) and that "stands" means to remain.

decisions.choice: "मरकर चली जाती है"; "हमेशा वहीं रहती है"
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, Readable says plainly that "goes" means to die (m2) and "stands" means to remain (m4).

decisions.choice: а
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the lines with "and", which here sets the lasting earth against the passing generations; Balanced and Readable say а. Literal keeps и.

decisions.choice: умирает
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that "goes" means to die (m2).

source.text: וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל־מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And rises the sun and goes the sun, and to its place panting, rising it there.

en.L: And the sun rises and the sun goes [down], \q and to its place it pants, [where] it rises there.
en.B: The sun rises and the sun sets, \q and it hurries back, panting, to the place where it rises again.
en.R: The sun comes up and the sun goes down. \q Then it rushes back to the place where it comes up again.

es.L: Y sale el sol, y se va el sol, \q y a su lugar jadea, [donde] allí sale.
es.B: El sol sale y el sol se pone, \q y vuelve de prisa, jadeando, al lugar donde sale otra vez.
es.R: El sol sale y el sol se pone. \q Luego corre de vuelta al lugar donde sale otra vez.

fr.L: Et le soleil se lève et le soleil s’en va, \q et vers son lieu il halète, [là où] il se lève.
fr.B: Le soleil se lève et le soleil se couche, \q puis il se hâte, haletant, vers le lieu où il se lève de nouveau.
fr.R: Le soleil se lève et le soleil se couche. \q Puis il court vite à l’endroit d’où il se lève encore.

sw.L: Jua linachomoza, na jua linatua, \q na kuelekea mahali pake linatweta, [mahali] linapochomoza huko.
sw.B: Jua linachomoza na jua linatua, \q kisha linaharakisha, likitweta, kurudi mahali linapochomoza tena.
sw.R: Jua linachomoza na jua linatua. \q Kisha linakimbia kurudi mahali linapochomoza tena.

vi.L: Và mặt trời mọc, và mặt trời lặn, \q và về chỗ của nó, nó thở hổn hển, [nơi] nó mọc lên ở đó.
vi.B: Mặt trời mọc rồi mặt trời lặn, \q và hối hả, thở hổn hển, trở về chỗ nó lại mọc lên.
vi.R: Mặt trời mọc lên rồi lặn xuống. \q Sau đó nó vội vã trở về chỗ để lại mọc lên.

ko.L: 해는 뜨고 해는 지며, \q 제자리로 헐떡이며 [가서] 거기서 떠오른다.
ko.B: 해는 뜨고 해는 지며, \q 다시 떠오를 그 자리로 헐떡이며 서둘러 돌아간다.
ko.R: 해가 떴다가 진다. \q 그러고는 다시 떠오를 곳으로 서둘러 돌아간다.

pt.L: E nasce o sol e se põe o sol, \q e para o seu lugar [vai] ofegante, ali onde nasce.
pt.B: O sol nasce e o sol se põe, \q e volta depressa, ofegante, ao lugar onde nasce outra vez.
pt.R: O sol aparece e o sol vai embora. \q Depois corre de volta para o lugar onde aparece de novo.

am.L: ፀሐይም ትወጣለች፤ ፀሐይም ትገባለች፤ \q ወደ ስፍራዋም ቁና ቁና እያለች [ትቸኩላለች]፤ በዚያም ትወጣለች።
am.B: ፀሐይ ትወጣለች፤ ፀሐይም ትጠልቃለች፤ \q እንደ ገና ወደምትወጣበት ስፍራ ቁና ቁና እያለች ትቸኩላለች።
am.R: ፀሐይ ትወጣለች፤ ፀሐይም ትጠልቃለች። \q ከዚያም እንደ ገና ወደምትወጣበት ስፍራ እየሮጠች ትመለሳለች።

hi.L: और सूर्य उगता है और सूर्य [डूब] जाता है, \q और अपने स्थान की ओर हाँफता हुआ [जाता है], [जहाँ] वह वहाँ उगता है।
hi.B: सूर्य उगता है और सूर्य डूबता है, \q और हाँफता हुआ जल्दी से उस स्थान को लौटता है जहाँ वह फिर उगता है।
hi.R: सूर्य निकलता है और सूर्य डूब जाता है। \q फिर वह जल्दी-जल्दी उसी जगह लौट जाता है जहाँ से वह फिर निकलता है।

ru.L: И восходит солнце, и заходит солнце, \q и к месту своему, задыхаясь, [спешит], там оно восходит.
ru.B: Солнце восходит, и солнце заходит, \q и, задыхаясь, спешит обратно к тому месту, где снова восходит.
ru.R: Солнце встаёт, и солнце садится, \q а потом торопится назад, туда, где снова встаёт.

ja.L: そして太陽は昇り、太陽は[沈んで]行く、 \q そしてそれが昇るその場所へと、あえぎながら[帰って行く]。
ja.B: 太陽は昇り、太陽は沈む。 \q そして、あえぎながら元の場所へ急いで戻り、そこからまた昇る。
ja.R: 太陽が昇り、太陽が沈む。 \q それから、また昇る場所へと急いで戻っていく。

uk.L: І сходить сонце, і заходить сонце, \q і до свого місця воно задихається, [де] воно сходить там.
uk.B: Сонце сходить і сонце заходить, \q і, задихаючись, поспішає назад, до місця, де знову сходить.
uk.R: Сонце сходить, і сонце заходить. \q Тоді воно поспішає назад, туди, де знову зійде.

decisions.choice: panting: gasping like a runner, perhaps from weariness, perhaps from eagerness
decisions.reason: The verb (sha'af) means to pant or gasp, as a woman in labor does (Isaiah 42:14), and also to long for something (Psalm 119:131). The sun is pictured as a runner who must get back to the starting place every night, to rise there again. Whether it pants from weariness or from eagerness is not said; Psalm 19:6 pictures it running its course with joy.

decisions.choice: goes: sets
decisions.reason: The verb (bo', "come in, go in") is used of the sun going down (Genesis 15:12).

decisions.choice: rising there: the place it hurries back to is the place where it rises
decisions.reason: The words are short and run on: the sun pants to its place, the place where it rises. Its daily course ends where it began.

decisions.choice: goes [down]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "down", which English needs to say that the sun sets.

decisions.choice: hurries back ... again (B); rushes back ... again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "panting" and adds "hurries back" to show where it pants to; Readable gives only the hurrying, the plain sense of the picture. "Again" brings out that the course repeats.

decisions.choice: "se va"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verb "go", which Spanish can say of the sun without an added word; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary "se pone".

decisions.choice: "se põe"
decisions.reason: Portuguese has its own verb for the setting sun, so Literal needs no bracket where the English supplies "[down]"; it brackets "[vai]" instead, which Portuguese needs before "ofegante".

decisions.choice: "ትገባለች" (L) for "goes"
decisions.reason: Amharic says the sun "goes in" ("ፀሐይ ገባች") when it sets, so Literal can keep the plain Hebrew verb of going without a bracket. Balanced and Readable say "ትጠልቃለች" (sets).

decisions.choice: "हाँफता हुआ जल्दी से ... लौटता है" (B); "जल्दी-जल्दी ... लौट जाता है" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced keeps "panting" and adds the hurrying back; Readable gives only the hurrying, the plain sense of the picture (m1, m3).

decisions.choice: [спешит]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that the sun pants toward its place (m1); Russian needs a verb of motion, which Literal brackets.

source.text: הוֹלֵךְ֙ אֶל־דָּר֔וֹם וְסוֹבֵ֖ב אֶל־צָפ֑וֹן סוֹבֵ֤ב׀סֹבֵב֙ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָר֔וּחַ וְעַל־סְבִיבֹתָ֖יו שָׁ֥ב הָרֽוּחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Going to [the] south and circling to [the] north, circling, circling, going the wind, and on its circuits returning the wind.

en.L: Going to [the] south and circling to [the] north, \q circling, circling goes the wind, \q and on its circuits the wind returns.
en.B: It blows to the south and turns to the north, \q round and round goes the wind, \q and on its rounds the wind comes back again.
en.R: The wind blows south, then it turns north. \q Round and round it goes, \q and it keeps coming back on the same paths.

es.L: Yendo hacia el sur y girando hacia el norte, \q girando, girando va el viento, \q y sobre sus giros vuelve el viento.
es.B: Sopla hacia el sur y gira hacia el norte; \q da vueltas y vueltas el viento, \q y en sus rondas el viento vuelve otra vez.
es.R: El viento sopla hacia el sur y luego gira al norte. \q Da vueltas y más vueltas, \q y siempre vuelve por los mismos caminos.

fr.L: Allant vers le sud et tournant vers le nord, \q tournant, tournant, va le vent, \q et sur ses circuits le vent revient.
fr.B: Il souffle vers le sud et tourne vers le nord ; \q il tourne et tourne encore, le vent, \q et sur ses tours le vent revient.
fr.R: Le vent souffle vers le sud, puis il tourne vers le nord. \q Il tourne et tourne encore, \q et il revient toujours par les mêmes chemins.

sw.L: Ukienda kusini na kuzunguka kaskazini, \q ukizunguka, ukizunguka, unakwenda upepo, \q na katika mizunguko yake upepo unarudi.
sw.B: Unavuma kuelekea kusini na kugeuka kuelekea kaskazini, \q unazunguka na kuzunguka, upepo, \q na katika mizunguko yake upepo unarudi tena.
sw.R: Upepo unavuma kusini, kisha unageuka kaskazini. \q Unazunguka na kuzunguka, \q na unaendelea kurudi katika njia zile zile.

vi.L: Đi về phương nam và xoay về phương bắc, \q xoay vòng, xoay vòng, gió cứ đi, \q và trên các vòng xoay của nó, gió trở lại.
vi.B: Nó thổi về phương nam rồi xoay sang phương bắc, \q gió cứ xoay vòng, xoay vòng mãi, \q và theo vòng xoay của mình, gió lại trở về.
vi.R: Gió thổi về hướng nam, rồi xoay sang hướng bắc. \q Nó cứ xoay vòng, xoay vòng, \q và cứ trở lại trên những con đường cũ.

ko.L: 남쪽으로 가고 북쪽으로 돌아, \q 돌고 돌며 바람이 가고, \q 그 도는 길 위로 바람이 돌아온다.
ko.B: 남쪽으로 불다가 북쪽으로 돌아서, \q 바람은 돌고 또 돌며, \q 그 돌던 길로 다시 돌아온다.
ko.R: 바람은 남쪽으로 불다가 북쪽으로 방향을 바꾼다. \q 바람은 돌고 또 돌아서, \q 늘 같은 길로 다시 돌아온다.

pt.L: Indo para o sul e girando para o norte, \q girando, girando vai o vento, \q e sobre os seus circuitos o vento volta.
pt.B: Sopra para o sul e vira para o norte, \q dando voltas e mais voltas vai o vento, \q e nas suas voltas o vento torna a passar.
pt.R: O vento sopra para o sul, depois vira para o norte. \q Dá voltas e mais voltas, \q e sempre volta pelos mesmos caminhos.

am.L: ወደ ደቡብ እየሄደ፣ ወደ ሰሜንም እየዞረ፣ \q እየዞረ እየዞረ ነፋሱ ይሄዳል፤ \q በዙረቱም ላይ ነፋሱ ይመለሳል።
am.B: ወደ ደቡብ ይነፍሳል፤ ወደ ሰሜንም ይዞራል፤ \q ነፋሱ እየዞረ እየዞረ ይሄዳል፤ \q በዙረቱም ነፋሱ ተመልሶ ይመጣል።
am.R: ነፋሱ ወደ ደቡብ ይነፍሳል፤ ከዚያም ወደ ሰሜን ይዞራል። \q ዙሪያውን እየዞረ ይሄዳል፤ \q በዚያው መንገዱም ተመልሶ ይመጣል።

hi.L: दक्षिण की ओर जाती हुई और उत्तर की ओर घूमती हुई, \q घूमती, घूमती जाती है हवा, \q और अपने चक्करों पर हवा लौटती है।
hi.B: वह दक्षिण की ओर बहती है और उत्तर की ओर मुड़ती है, \q गोल-गोल घूमती जाती है हवा, \q और अपने चक्करों पर हवा फिर लौट आती है।
hi.R: हवा दक्षिण की ओर बहती है, फिर उत्तर की ओर मुड़ जाती है। \q वह गोल-गोल घूमती रहती है, \q और बार-बार उन्हीं रास्तों पर लौट आती है।

ru.L: Идёт на юг и кружит на север, \q кружит, кружит, идёт ветер, \q и по своим кругам ветер возвращается.
ru.B: Дует на юг и поворачивает на север, \q кругом, кругом идёт ветер, \q и по своим кругам ветер возвращается снова.
ru.R: Ветер дует на юг, потом поворачивает на север. \q Он кружит и кружит \q и всё время возвращается на те же пути.

ja.L: 南へと行き、北へと巡る、 \q 巡りに巡って風は行き、 \q その巡る道の上を風は帰る。
ja.B: 南に吹き、北へと向きを変える。 \q 風はぐるぐると巡り、 \q 巡りながら、また元の所へ戻って来る。
ja.R: 風は南に吹き、それから北へ向きを変える。 \q ぐるぐると回り続け、 \q 何度も同じ道を通って戻って来る。

uk.L: Іде на південь і кружляє на північ, \q кружляє, кружляє, іде вітер, \q і на свої кола вітер вертається.
uk.B: Віє на південь і повертає на північ, \q кружляє й кружляє вітер \q і на свої кола знову вертається.
uk.R: Вітер віє на південь, потім повертає на північ. \q Він кружляє й кружляє \q і весь час вертається тими самими шляхами.

decisions.choice: the wind: named only after two lines
alternatives: the sun, still the subject of the first words
decisions.reason: The opening words could at first be heard of the sun, which moves toward the south and the north through the year. Only in the second line is the subject named: the wind. The Hebrew holds it back, so that sun and wind run together in one picture of endless circling.

decisions.choice: wind: moving air
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) can mean wind, breath or spirit. Here it is the wind that blows over the land, the same word as in "a chasing of wind" (1:14).

decisions.choice: circling, circling: the word is repeated to show motion without end
decisions.reason: The participle "circling" is said three times in the verse, and "circuits" comes from the same root. The wind is always moving and never arrives anywhere new.

decisions.choice: turns ... round and round ... rounds
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the plain English "round and round" for the repeated participle; Literal keeps "circling" each time.

decisions.choice: keeps coming back on the same paths
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "its circuits" are: the same routes, over and over.

decisions.choice: "바람" held back to the second line
alternatives: "바람이" at the start of the verse
decisions.reason: Korean can leave a subject unspoken, so Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's delay: the first line could still be the sun until the wind is named (m1). Readable names the wind first.

decisions.choice: "गोल-गोल"
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the everyday Hindi doubling for the repeated participle (m3); Literal keeps "घूमती, घूमती". As in the Hebrew, Literal and Balanced name the wind only in the second line (m1).

decisions.choice: возвращается на те же пути
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "its circuits" are: the same routes, over and over.

source.text: כָּל־הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹלְכִ֣ים אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם וְהַיָּ֖ם אֵינֶ֣נּוּ מָלֵ֑א אֶל־מְק֗וֹם שֶׁ֤הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹֽלְכִ֔ים שָׁ֛ם הֵ֥ם שָׁבִ֖ים לָלָֽכֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: All the streams going to the sea, and the sea, it is not full; to the place which the streams going, there they returning to go.

en.L: All the streams go to the sea, \q and the sea is not full; \q to the place where the streams go, \q there they return to go [again].
en.B: All the streams run to the sea, \q yet the sea is never full; \q to the place where the streams run, \q there they keep on running.
en.R: All the rivers flow into the sea, \q but the sea never fills up. \q The rivers keep flowing to the same place again and again.

es.L: Todos los torrentes van al mar, \q y el mar no está lleno; \q al lugar adonde van los torrentes, \q allí vuelven para ir [de nuevo].
es.B: Todos los ríos corren al mar, \q y sin embargo el mar nunca se llena; \q al lugar adonde corren los ríos, \q allí siguen corriendo.
es.R: Todos los ríos van a dar al mar, \q pero el mar nunca se llena. \q Los ríos siguen corriendo al mismo lugar una y otra vez.

fr.L: Tous les torrents vont vers la mer, \q et la mer n’est pas pleine ; \q vers le lieu où vont les torrents, \q là ils retournent pour aller [encore].
fr.B: Tous les cours d’eau courent vers la mer, \q et pourtant la mer n’est jamais pleine ; \q vers le lieu où courent les cours d’eau, \q là ils ne cessent de courir.
fr.R: Toutes les rivières se jettent dans la mer, \q mais la mer ne se remplit jamais. \q Les rivières continuent de couler vers le même endroit, encore et encore.

sw.L: Vijito vyote vinakwenda baharini, \q na bahari haijai; \q mahali vijito vinapokwenda, \q huko vinarudi kwenda [tena].
sw.B: Mito yote inatiririka kwenda baharini, \q lakini bahari haijai kamwe; \q mahali mito inapotiririka, \q huko inaendelea kutiririka.
sw.R: Mito yote inaingia baharini, \q lakini bahari haijai kamwe. \q Mito inaendelea kutiririka mahali pale pale tena na tena.

vi.L: Mọi dòng suối đều chảy ra biển, \q và biển không đầy; \q về nơi các dòng suối chảy đến, \q ở đó chúng trở lại để chảy [nữa].
vi.B: Mọi dòng sông đều chảy ra biển, \q vậy mà biển chẳng bao giờ đầy; \q về nơi các dòng sông chảy đến, \q ở đó chúng cứ chảy mãi.
vi.R: Mọi con sông đều đổ ra biển, \q nhưng biển không bao giờ đầy. \q Sông cứ chảy về cùng một nơi, hết lần này đến lần khác.

ko.L: 모든 시내가 바다로 가도 \q 바다는 차지 않는다. \q 시내들이 가는 그곳, \q 그곳으로 [또] 가려고 돌아간다.
ko.B: 모든 강물이 바다로 흘러가도 \q 바다는 결코 가득 차지 않는다. \q 강물은 흘러가던 그곳으로 \q 계속해서 흘러간다.
ko.R: 모든 강이 바다로 흘러가지만, \q 바다는 가득 차는 법이 없다. \q 강물은 같은 곳으로 흐르고 또 흐른다.

pt.L: Todos os riachos vão para o mar, \q e o mar não está cheio; \q para o lugar aonde os riachos vão, \q ali eles voltam a ir.
pt.B: Todos os córregos correm para o mar, \q e mesmo assim o mar nunca fica cheio; \q para o lugar aonde os córregos correm, \q para lá continuam correndo.
pt.R: Todos os rios desembocam no mar, \q mas o mar nunca enche. \q Os rios continuam correndo para o mesmo lugar, de novo e de novo.

am.L: ወንዞች ሁሉ ወደ ባሕር ይሄዳሉ፤ \q ባሕሩም አይሞላም፤ \q ወንዞቹ ወደሚሄዱበት ስፍራ፣ \q ወደዚያ [እንደ ገና] ለመሄድ ይመለሳሉ።
am.B: ወንዞች ሁሉ ወደ ባሕር ይፈስሳሉ፤ \q ባሕሩ ግን ፈጽሞ አይሞላም፤ \q ወንዞቹ ወደሚፈስሱበት ስፍራ፣ \q ወደዚያው መፍሰሳቸውን አያቋርጡም።
am.R: ወንዞች ሁሉ ወደ ባሕር ይፈስሳሉ፤ \q ባሕሩ ግን ከቶ አይሞላም። \q ወንዞቹ ደጋግመው ወደዚያው ስፍራ ይፈስሳሉ።

hi.L: सब नदियाँ समुद्र की ओर जाती हैं, \q और समुद्र भरता नहीं; \q जिस स्थान को नदियाँ जाती हैं, \q वहीं वे [फिर] जाने को लौटती हैं।
hi.B: सब नदियाँ समुद्र की ओर बहती हैं, \q फिर भी समुद्र कभी नहीं भरता; \q जिस स्थान को नदियाँ बहती हैं, \q वहीं वे बहती ही रहती हैं।
hi.R: सारी नदियाँ समुद्र में जा मिलती हैं, \q पर समुद्र कभी भरता नहीं। \q नदियाँ बार-बार उसी जगह की ओर बहती रहती हैं।

ru.L: Все потоки идут в море, \q а море не полно; \q к месту, куда потоки идут, \q туда они возвращаются, чтобы идти [снова].
ru.B: Все реки бегут в море, \q но море никогда не переполняется; \q к месту, куда бегут реки, \q туда они и бегут без конца.
ru.R: Все реки впадают в море, \q но море никогда не наполняется. \q Реки снова и снова текут туда же.

ja.L: すべての川は海へ行く、 \q そして海は満ちない。 \q 川が行くその場所へ、 \q そこへそれらは[再び]行くために帰る。
ja.B: 川はみな海に流れ込む。 \q しかし、海はあふれることがない。 \q 川が流れて行くその場所へ、 \q 川はいつまでも流れ続ける。
ja.R: 川はみな海に流れ込む。 \q でも、海はいっぱいにならない。 \q 川は何度も何度も同じ所へ流れていく。

uk.L: Усі потоки йдуть до моря, \q а море не повне; \q до місця, куди потоки йдуть, \q туди вони вертаються, щоб іти [знову].
uk.B: Усі потоки біжать до моря, \q але море ніколи не наповнюється; \q до місця, куди біжать потоки, \q туди вони й далі біжать.
uk.R: Усі ріки течуть у море, \q але море ніколи не переповнюється. \q Ріки знову й знову течуть до того самого місця.

decisions.choice: streams: river valleys and the water that runs in them
decisions.reason: The word (nachal) is a stream bed or valley that runs with water, often only in the rainy season, as well as a flowing stream (Numbers 34:5; 1 Kings 17:7).

decisions.choice: there they return to go: they keep going there, over and over
alternatives: they go back from there to flow again
decisions.reason: The words can mean that the streams keep flowing to the same place, or that they go back to where they began in order to flow again. Either way the picture is endless motion that fills nothing.

decisions.choice: [again]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "again", which English needs to make sense of "return to go".

decisions.choice: keep on running (B); keep flowing ... again and again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the Hebrew pair means in the reading taken (m2).

decisions.choice: ali eles voltam a ir
alternatives: ali eles voltam a ir [de novo]
decisions.reason: Portuguese "voltar a" already means "do again", so Literal needs no bracket where the English supplies "[again]".

decisions.choice: [снова]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets снова, which Russian needs to make sense of "return to go" (m2).

source.text: כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים יְגֵעִ֔ים לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל אִ֖ישׁ לְדַבֵּ֑ר לֹא־תִשְׂבַּ֥ע עַ֨יִן֙ לִרְא֔וֹת וְלֹא־תִמָּלֵ֥א אֹ֖זֶן מִשְּׁמֹֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: All the things [are] wearisome; not able a man to speak; not satisfied an eye with seeing, and not filled an ear from hearing.

en.L: All things [are] wearisome; \q no one is able to speak [of it]; \q the eye is not satisfied with seeing, \q and the ear is not filled with hearing.
en.B: Everything is wearisome, \q more than anyone can say; \q the eye is never satisfied with seeing, \q and the ear is never filled with hearing.
en.R: Everything wears people out, more than anyone can say. \q Our eyes never see enough, and our ears never hear enough.

es.L: Todas las cosas [son] fatigosas; \q nadie puede hablar [de ello]; \q no se sacia el ojo de ver, \q ni se llena el oído de oír.
es.B: Todo es fatigoso, \q más de lo que nadie puede decir; \q el ojo nunca se sacia de ver, \q ni el oído se llena de oír.
es.R: Todo cansa a la gente, más de lo que nadie puede decir. \q Nuestros ojos nunca ven bastante, y nuestros oídos nunca oyen bastante.

fr.L: Toutes les choses [sont] lassantes ; \q nul ne peut [en] parler ; \q l’œil ne se rassasie pas de voir, \q et l’oreille ne se remplit pas d’entendre.
fr.B: Tout est lassant, \q plus qu’on ne saurait le dire ; \q l’œil n’est jamais rassasié de voir, \q et l’oreille n’est jamais remplie d’entendre.
fr.R: Tout fatigue les gens, plus qu’on ne peut le dire. \q Nos yeux n’en voient jamais assez, et nos oreilles n’en entendent jamais assez.

sw.L: Mambo yote [ni] ya kuchosha; \q hakuna mtu awezaye kuyasema; \q jicho halishibi kuona, \q wala sikio halijai kwa kusikia.
sw.B: Kila kitu kinachosha, \q kuliko mtu yeyote awezavyo kusema; \q jicho halishibi kuona kamwe, \q wala sikio halijai kwa kusikia.
sw.R: Kila kitu kinawachosha watu, kuliko mtu yeyote awezavyo kusema. \q Macho yetu hayatosheki kuona, na masikio yetu hayatosheki kusikia.

vi.L: Mọi sự [đều] mệt mỏi; \q không ai có thể nói [hết]; \q mắt không no nê vì thấy, \q và tai không đầy vì nghe.
vi.B: Mọi sự đều làm mệt mỏi, \q hơn cả điều người ta có thể nói; \q mắt chẳng bao giờ nhìn cho thỏa, \q tai chẳng bao giờ nghe cho đầy.
vi.R: Mọi sự đều làm con người mệt mỏi, mệt đến không nói hết được. \q Mắt chúng ta chẳng bao giờ nhìn cho đủ, tai chúng ta chẳng bao giờ nghe cho đủ.

ko.L: 모든 것이 피곤하니, \q 사람이 [그것을] 다 말할 수 없다. \q 눈은 보아도 만족하지 않고, \q 귀는 들어도 차지 않는다.
ko.B: 모든 것이 피곤하여 \q 누구도 다 말할 수 없다. \q 눈은 보고 또 보아도 만족하지 못하고, \q 귀는 듣고 또 들어도 채워지지 않는다.
ko.R: 모든 것이 사람을 지치게 한다. 말로 다 할 수 없을 만큼 지치게 한다. \q 우리 눈은 아무리 보아도 만족하지 못하고, 우리 귀는 아무리 들어도 만족하지 못한다.

pt.L: Todas as coisas [são] cansativas; \q ninguém consegue falar [delas]; \q o olho não se sacia de ver, \q e o ouvido não se enche de ouvir.
pt.B: Tudo é cansativo, \q mais do que alguém consegue dizer; \q o olho nunca se satisfaz de ver, \q e o ouvido nunca se enche de ouvir.
pt.R: Tudo cansa as pessoas, mais do que alguém consegue dizer. \q Os nossos olhos nunca veem o bastante, e os nossos ouvidos nunca ouvem o bastante.

am.L: ነገሮች ሁሉ አድካሚ [ናቸው]፤ \q ሰው [ስለ እርሱ] ሊናገር አይችልም፤ \q ዓይን በማየት አትጠግብም፤ \q ጆሮም በመስማት አትሞላም።
am.B: ሁሉም ነገር አድካሚ ነው፤ \q ማንም ሊናገረው ከሚችለው በላይ ነው፤ \q ዓይን በማየት ፈጽሞ አትጠግብም፤ \q ጆሮም በመስማት ፈጽሞ አትሞላም።
am.R: ሁሉም ነገር ሰዎችን ያደክማል፤ ማንም ሊገልጸው ከሚችለው በላይ ነው። \q ዓይኖቻችን አይተው አይጠግቡም፤ ጆሮዎቻችንም ሰምተው አይጠግቡም።

hi.L: सब बातें थकानेवाली [हैं]; \q कोई मनुष्य [उनका] वर्णन नहीं कर सकता; \q आँख देखने से तृप्त नहीं होती, \q और कान सुनने से भरता नहीं।
hi.B: सब कुछ थका देनेवाला है, \q जितना कोई कह सके उससे भी अधिक; \q आँख देखने से कभी तृप्त नहीं होती, \q और कान सुनने से कभी नहीं भरता।
hi.R: सब कुछ लोगों को इतना थका देता है कि कोई कह भी नहीं सकता। \q हमारी आँखें कभी जी भरकर नहीं देखतीं, और हमारे कान कभी जी भरकर नहीं सुनते।

ru.L: Все вещи утомительны; \q не может человек высказать [этого]; \q глаз не насыщается тем, что видит, \q и ухо не наполняется тем, что слышит.
ru.B: Всё утомляет \q больше, чем можно выразить словами; \q глаз никогда не насытится увиденным, \q и ухо никогда не наполнится услышанным.
ru.R: Всё изматывает людей сильнее, чем можно сказать. \q Наши глаза никогда не насмотрятся, а уши никогда не наслушаются.

ja.L: すべての物事は疲れに満ちている、 \q 人は[それを]語り尽くすことができない。 \q 目は見ることに満ち足りず、 \q 耳は聞くことで満たされない。
ja.B: すべてのことは人を疲れさせ、 \q だれにも言い尽くせない。 \q 目は見ても見飽きることがなく、 \q 耳は聞いても聞き飽きることがない。
ja.R: すべてのことが人を疲れさせる。言葉では言い表せないほどだ。 \q わたしたちの目はいくら見ても足りず、耳はいくら聞いても足りない。

uk.L: Усі речі виснажливі; \q ніхто не може [про це] сказати; \q не насититься око баченням, \q і не наповниться вухо слуханням.
uk.B: Усе виснажливе, \q більше, ніж можна висловити; \q око ніколи не насититься баченим, \q і вухо ніколи не наповниться почутим.
uk.R: Усе виснажує людей більше, ніж можна сказати. \q Наші очі ніколи не надивляться, а вуха ніколи не наслухаються.

decisions.choice: all things are wearisome: everything goes on without rest and wearies those who try to grasp it
alternatives: all words are weary: speech gives out before the matter is told
decisions.reason: The noun (davar) means "word" or "thing", and the adjective (yagea') "weary" or "wearying". The sun, the wind and the streams labor and never rest, and all of it wears out a person who tries to grasp it or tell it. The words could also mean that words themselves grow weary: speech runs out before the matter is told.

decisions.choice: no one is able to speak: the matter is beyond telling
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the sense is that no one can put it all into words. The word for "one" ('ish) means anyone.

decisions.choice: the eye is not satisfied: desire is never filled
decisions.reason: Proverbs says the same of human eyes (Proverbs 27:20), and the book returns to it in 4:8 and 6:7. Eye and ear take in more and more, as the sea takes in the streams, and are never full.

decisions.choice: more than anyone can say
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the short clause to what goes before, as the reading taken in m2 implies.

decisions.choice: Our eyes ... our ears
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of "our" eyes and ears to make the general statement plain.

decisions.choice: "जी भरकर नहीं देखतीं ... नहीं सुनते"
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday Hindi "जी भरकर" for being satisfied (m3), and speaks of "our" eyes and ears as the English does.

decisions.choice: насмотрятся ... наслушаются
decisions.reason: Readable uses the Russian verbs for having seen and heard one's fill, which say the never-filled desire (m3) in everyday words.

source.text: מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ ה֣וּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֔ה וּמַה־שֶׁנַּֽעֲשָׂ֔ה ה֖וּא שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין כָּל־חָדָ֖שׁ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: What has been, it [is] what will be, and what has been done, it [is] what will be done; and there is not any new [thing] under the sun.

en.L: What has been, it [is] what will be, \q and what has been done, it [is] what will be done, \q and there is nothing new under the sun.
en.B: What has been is what will be, \q and what has been done is what will be done; \q there is nothing new under the sun.
en.R: Whatever has happened will happen again. \q Whatever people have done, they will do again. \q There is nothing new in this world.

es.L: Lo que ha sido, eso [es] lo que será, \q y lo que se ha hecho, eso [es] lo que se hará, \q y no hay nada nuevo bajo el sol.
es.B: Lo que ha sido es lo que será, \q y lo que se ha hecho es lo que se hará; \q no hay nada nuevo bajo el sol.
es.R: Todo lo que ha pasado volverá a pasar. \q Todo lo que la gente ha hecho, lo volverá a hacer. \q No hay nada nuevo en este mundo.

fr.L: Ce qui a été, cela [est] ce qui sera, \q et ce qui a été fait, cela [est] ce qui sera fait, \q et il n’y a rien de nouveau sous le soleil.
fr.B: Ce qui a existé existera encore, \q ce qui a été fait se fera encore ; \q rien n’est nouveau sous le soleil.
fr.R: Tout ce qui est arrivé arrivera encore. \q Tout ce que les gens ont fait, ils le feront encore. \q Il n’y a rien de nouveau dans ce monde.

sw.L: Kile kilichokuwa, hicho [ndicho] kitakachokuwa, \q na kile kilichotendwa, hicho [ndicho] kitakachotendwa, \q wala hakuna jipya lolote chini ya jua.
sw.B: Kilichokuwa ndicho kitakachokuwa, \q na kilichofanyika ndicho kitakachofanyika; \q hakuna kitu kipya chini ya jua.
sw.R: Kila kilichotokea kitatokea tena. \q Kila ambacho watu wamefanya, watakifanya tena. \q Hakuna kitu kipya hapa duniani.

vi.L: Điều đã có, [chính] nó là điều sẽ có, \q và điều đã làm, [chính] nó là điều sẽ làm, \q và chẳng có gì mới dưới mặt trời.
vi.B: Những gì đã có là những gì sẽ có, \q những gì đã làm là những gì sẽ làm; \q chẳng có gì mới dưới mặt trời.
vi.R: Chuyện gì đã xảy ra sẽ lại xảy ra. \q Việc gì người ta đã làm, họ sẽ lại làm. \q Trên đời này chẳng có gì mới cả.

ko.L: 있었던 것, 그것이 있을 것이고, \q 이루어진 것, 그것이 이루어질 것이니, \q 해 아래에 새것이란 없다.
ko.B: 있었던 것이 다시 있을 것이고, \q 이루어진 일이 다시 이루어질 것이다. \q 해 아래에 새로운 것은 하나도 없다.
ko.R: 일어난 일은 또다시 일어난다. \q 사람들이 한 일은 또다시 하게 된다. \q 이 세상에 새로운 것은 아무것도 없다.

pt.L: O que foi, isso [é] o que será, \q e o que foi feito, isso [é] o que será feito, \q e não há nada novo debaixo do sol.
pt.B: O que já existiu é o que vai existir, \q e o que já se fez é o que se fará; \q não há nada de novo debaixo do sol.
pt.R: Tudo o que aconteceu vai acontecer de novo. \q Tudo o que as pessoas fizeram, elas vão fazer de novo. \q Não há nada de novo neste mundo.

am.L: የነበረው እርሱ የሚሆነው [ነው]፤ \q የተደረገውም እርሱ የሚደረገው [ነው]፤ \q ከፀሐይ በታችም አዲስ ነገር የለም።
am.B: የነበረው ወደፊትም የሚሆነው ነው፤ \q የተደረገውም ወደፊት የሚደረገው ነው፤ \q ከፀሐይ በታች አዲስ ነገር የለም።
am.R: የሆነው ሁሉ እንደ ገና ይሆናል። \q ሰዎች ያደረጉትን ሁሉ እንደ ገና ያደርጉታል። \q በዚህ ዓለም አዲስ ነገር የለም።

hi.L: जो हुआ है, वही [है] जो होगा, \q और जो किया गया है, वही [है] जो किया जाएगा, \q और सूर्य के नीचे कुछ भी नया नहीं।
hi.B: जो हो चुका है, वही फिर होगा, \q और जो किया जा चुका है, वही फिर किया जाएगा; \q सूर्य के नीचे कुछ भी नया नहीं है।
hi.R: जो कुछ हुआ है, वह फिर होगा। \q लोगों ने जो कुछ किया है, वे उसे फिर करेंगे। \q सूर्य के नीचे कुछ भी नया नहीं है।

ru.L: То, что было, — это то, что будет, \q и то, что сделано, — это то, что будет сделано, \q и нет ничего нового под солнцем.
ru.B: Что было прежде, то будет и впредь, \q что делали прежде, то будут делать и впредь; \q под солнцем нет ничего нового.
ru.R: Всё, что случилось, случится снова. \q Всё, что люди сделали, они сделают снова. \q Под солнцем нет ничего нового.

ja.L: あったこと、それはあるであろうこと、 \q なされたこと、それはなされるであろうこと、 \q そして太陽の下に新しいものは何一つない。
ja.B: かつてあったことは、これからもあり、 \q かつてなされたことは、これからもなされる。 \q 太陽の下に新しいものは何もない。
ja.R: 起こったことは、また起こる。 \q 人がしたことは、またする。 \q この世に新しいものは何もない。

uk.L: Що було, те [й] буде, \q і що робилося, те [й] робитиметься, \q і немає нічого нового під сонцем.
uk.B: Що було, те й буде, \q і що робилося, те й робитиметься; \q немає нічого нового під сонцем.
uk.R: Що вже сталося, те станеться знову. \q Що люди вже робили, те робитимуть знову. \q У цьому світі немає нічого нового.

decisions.choice: what has been ... what will be: the future repeats the past
decisions.reason: The first pair speaks of what happens, the second of what is done. Like the sun, wind and streams of verses 5-7, events and deeds come round again.

decisions.choice: nothing new under the sun: nothing in human life is truly new
decisions.reason: The claim is about the world of human experience (see the note on "under the sun" at 1:3). Verse 10 takes up the obvious objection.

decisions.choice: in this world
decisions.reason: Readable's wording for "under the sun" (see 1:3).

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "what has been done" without naming who does it. Readable names people as the ones who act, since the line is about human deeds.
As the English Readable, Readable names people as the ones who act. "सूर्य के नीचे" stays at Readable too (see 1:3).

decisions.choice: люди
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "what has been done" without naming who does it; Readable names people, since the line is about human deeds.

source.text: יֵ֥שׁ דָּבָ֛ר שֶׁיֹּאמַ֥ר רְאֵה־זֶ֖ה חָדָ֣שׁ ה֑וּא כְּבָר֙ הָיָ֣ה לְעֹֽלָמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה מִלְּפָנֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is there a thing which one says, See this, new it [is]? Already it has been for ages which were before us.

en.L: Is there a thing of which one says, "See this, it [is] new"? \q Already it has been in the ages that were before us.
en.B: Is there anything of which people say, "Look, this is new"? \q It was already here long ages before us.
en.R: People may say, "Look! This is something new!" \q But it was already here long before our time.

es.L: ¿Hay una cosa de la que se diga: «Mira esto, [es] nuevo»? \q Ya existió en las edades que hubo antes de nosotros.
es.B: ¿Hay algo de lo que la gente diga: «Mira, esto es nuevo»? \q Ya existía mucho tiempo antes de nosotros.
es.R: Puede que la gente diga: «¡Mira! ¡Esto es algo nuevo!». \q Pero ya existía mucho antes de nuestro tiempo.

fr.L: Y a-t-il une chose dont on dise : « Vois ceci, [c’est] nouveau » ? \q Déjà elle a été dans les âges qui étaient avant nous.
fr.B: Y a-t-il une chose dont on dise : « Regarde, voici du nouveau » ? \q Elle existait déjà bien des siècles avant nous.
fr.R: Les gens disent parfois : « Regarde ! C’est quelque chose de nouveau ! » \q Mais cela existait déjà bien avant nous.

sw.L: Je, kuna jambo ambalo mtu atasema, "Tazama hili, [ni] jipya"? \q Tayari limekuwapo katika nyakati zilizokuwa kabla yetu.
sw.B: Je, kuna jambo lolote ambalo watu husema, "Tazama, hili ni jipya"? \q Lilikuwapo tayari zamani sana kabla yetu.
sw.R: Watu wanaweza kusema, "Tazama! Hiki ni kitu kipya!" \q Lakini kilikuwapo tayari muda mrefu kabla ya wakati wetu.

vi.L: Có điều gì mà người ta nói: "Hãy xem điều này, nó [là] mới"? \q Nó đã có rồi trong những thời đại trước chúng ta.
vi.B: Có điều gì mà người ta bảo: "Kìa, cái này mới đấy"? \q Nó đã có từ bao đời trước chúng ta rồi.
vi.R: Người ta có thể nói: "Xem kìa! Cái này mới đấy!" \q Nhưng nó đã có từ lâu, trước thời của chúng ta.

ko.L: "보라, 이것은 새것이다" 하고 말할 만한 것이 있는가? \q 그것은 우리 앞에 있던 오랜 세대에 이미 있었다.
ko.B: 사람들이 "보아라, 이건 새로운 것이다" 하고 말하는 것이 있는가? \q 그것은 우리보다 훨씬 오래전에 이미 있었다.
ko.R: 사람들은 "봐! 이건 새로운 거야!" 하고 말할지도 모른다. \q 그러나 그것은 우리가 살기 훨씬 전부터 이미 있었다.

pt.L: Há uma coisa da qual se diz: "Veja isto, isto [é] novo"? \q Já existiu nas eras que foram antes de nós.
pt.B: Existe alguma coisa de que as pessoas dizem: "Olhe, isto é novo"? \q Já estava aqui longas eras antes de nós.
pt.R: As pessoas podem dizer: "Olhe! Isto é uma coisa nova!" \q Mas já existia muito antes do nosso tempo.

am.L: ሰው፦ «ይህን እይ፤ አዲስ [ነው]» የሚልለት ነገር አለን? \q ከእኛ በፊት በነበሩት ዘመናት አስቀድሞ ነበረ።
am.B: ሰዎች፦ «ተመልከቱ፤ ይህ አዲስ ነው» የሚሉት ነገር አለን? \q ከእኛ ከብዙ ዘመናት በፊት አስቀድሞ ነበረ።
am.R: ሰዎች «ተመልከቱ! ይህ አዲስ ነገር ነው!» ይሉ ይሆናል። \q ነገር ግን ከእኛ ዘመን ብዙ አስቀድሞ ነበረ።

hi.L: क्या कोई बात है जिसके विषय में कोई कहे, "देखो, यह नया [है]"? \q वह तो उन युगों में पहले ही हो चुकी है जो हमसे पहले थे।
hi.B: क्या कोई ऐसी बात है जिसके विषय में लोग कहें, "देखो, यह नया है"? \q वह तो हमसे युगों पहले ही यहाँ थी।
hi.R: लोग कह सकते हैं, "देखो! यह तो कुछ नया है!" \q पर वह हमारे समय से बहुत पहले ही यहाँ था।

ru.L: Есть ли вещь, о которой скажут: «Смотри, это — новое»? \q Это уже было в веках, что были до нас.
ru.B: Есть ли что-нибудь, о чём люди говорят: «Смотри, вот новое»? \q Оно уже было здесь задолго до нас, в давние века.
ru.R: Люди могут сказать: «Смотри! Вот что-то новое!» \q Но это уже было задолго до нашего времени.

ja.L: 「これを見よ、これは新しい」と人が言うような事柄があるだろうか？ \q それは、わたしたちより前の遠い時代に、すでにあった。
ja.B: 「見てごらん、これは新しいものだ」と言われるようなものがあるだろうか？ \q それは、わたしたちよりずっと前の時代から、すでにあった。
ja.R: 人は「見て！これは新しいものだ！」と言うかもしれない。 \q しかし、それはわたしたちの時代よりずっと前からあった。

uk.L: Чи є річ, про яку кажуть: «Подивись на це, воно нове»? \q Воно вже було у віках, які були перед нами.
uk.B: Чи є щось, про що люди кажуть: «Дивіться, це нове»? \q Воно вже було задовго до нас, у давніх віках.
uk.R: Люди можуть сказати: «Дивіться! Ось щось нове!» \q Але воно вже було задовго до нас.

decisions.choice: is there a thing: a question that grants the claim might be made, only to answer it
decisions.reason: The question allows that people will point to something as new. The second line answers: it has been before.

decisions.choice: ages: long times past
decisions.reason: The plural of 'olam means long ages, here reaching back into the past (compare Psalm 77:6).

decisions.choice: People may say
alternatives: Is there anything of which people say
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a plain statement with the same point.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the words people say
decisions.reason: Qoheleth's own voice takes no quotation marks; speech he quotes inside it takes double quotes.

decisions.choice: the quoted words first: "\"보라, 이것은 새것이다\" 하고 말할 만한 것이 있는가?"
decisions.reason: Korean puts a quotation before the verb that introduces it, so the words people say come first in the line; the Hebrew question about "a thing" follows.

decisions.choice: «...» for the words people say
decisions.reason: Qoheleth's own voice takes no quotation marks; speech he quotes inside it takes «», as in the English.

source.text: אֵ֥ין זִכְר֖וֹן לָרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וְגַ֨ם לָאַחֲרֹנִ֜ים שֶׁיִּהְי֗וּ לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ זִכָּר֔וֹן עִ֥ם שֶׁיִּהְי֖וּ לָאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: There is not remembrance of the former [ones], and also of the latter [ones] who will be, there will not be for them remembrance with those who will be at the latter [time].

en.L: There is no remembrance of the former [ones]; \q and also of the later [ones] who will be, there will be no remembrance of them \q with those who will be at the last.
en.B: No one remembers those who came before, \q and those who are yet to come \q will not be remembered by those who come after them.
en.R: No one remembers the people who lived long ago. \q And the people still to come will be forgotten by those who live after them.

es.L: No hay recuerdo de los de antes; \q y tampoco de los de después, que vendrán, habrá recuerdo de ellos \q entre los que vendrán al final.
es.B: Nadie recuerda a los que vinieron antes, \q y a los que aún han de venir \q tampoco los recordarán los que vengan después.
es.R: Nadie se acuerda de la gente que vivió hace mucho. \q Y a los que todavía han de venir, los olvidarán los que vivan después de ellos.

fr.L: Il n’y a pas de souvenir des premiers ; \q et aussi des derniers qui seront, il n’y aura pas de souvenir d’eux \q chez ceux qui seront à la fin.
fr.B: Personne ne se souvient de ceux d’autrefois, \q et ceux qui sont encore à venir, \q ceux qui viendront après eux ne s’en souviendront pas.
fr.R: Personne ne se souvient des gens qui ont vécu il y a longtemps. \q Et ceux qui vont venir seront oubliés par ceux qui vivront après eux.

sw.L: Hakuna kumbukumbu ya [watu] wa kwanza; \q na pia ya wale wa mwisho watakaokuwako, hakutakuwa na kumbukumbu yao \q kwa wale watakaokuwako mwishoni.
sw.B: Hakuna anayewakumbuka wale waliotangulia, \q na wale ambao bado watakuja \q hawatakumbukwa na wale watakaokuja baada yao.
sw.R: Hakuna anayewakumbuka watu walioishi zamani. \q Na watu watakaokuja watasahauliwa na wale watakaoishi baada yao.

vi.L: Không có sự ghi nhớ về những [người] trước; \q và cả những [người] sau sẽ đến, cũng sẽ không có sự ghi nhớ về họ \q nơi những người sẽ có về sau.
vi.B: Không ai nhớ đến những người đi trước, \q và những người còn sẽ đến \q cũng sẽ không được những người đến sau nhớ đến.
vi.R: Chẳng ai nhớ đến những người sống từ xưa. \q Và những người sắp đến cũng sẽ bị những người sống sau họ quên đi.

ko.L: 이전 [사람들]에 대한 기억이 없고, \q 앞으로 있을 나중 [사람들]에 대해서도 그들에 대한 기억이 \q 마지막 때에 있을 자들에게 없을 것이다.
ko.B: 앞서 간 사람들을 기억하는 이가 없고, \q 아직 오지 않은 사람들도 \q 그 뒤에 올 사람들이 기억하지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 오래전에 살았던 사람들을 기억하는 사람은 없다. \q 앞으로 올 사람들도 그 뒤에 살 사람들에게 잊힐 것이다.

pt.L: Não há memória dos primeiros; \q e também dos últimos que virão, não haverá memória deles \q entre os que virão no fim.
pt.B: Ninguém se lembra dos que vieram antes, \q e os que ainda vão vir \q não serão lembrados pelos que vierem depois deles.
pt.R: Ninguém se lembra das pessoas que viveram há muito tempo. \q E as pessoas que ainda vão nascer serão esquecidas pelos que vierem depois delas.

am.L: ለቀደሙት መታሰቢያ የለም፤ \q ደግሞም ለሚመጡት ለኋለኞቹ መታሰቢያ አይሆንላቸውም \q በመጨረሻ ከሚመጡት ዘንድ።
am.B: ቀድመው የነበሩትን ማንም አያስታውሳቸውም፤ \q ገና የሚመጡትም \q ከእነርሱ በኋላ በሚመጡት አይታሰቡም።
am.R: ከብዙ ዘመን በፊት የኖሩትን ሰዎች ማንም አያስታውሳቸውም። \q ገና የሚመጡትም ሰዎች ከእነርሱ በኋላ በሚኖሩት ይረሳሉ።

hi.L: पहलेवालों का कोई स्मरण नहीं; \q और बादवालों का भी, जो होंगे, कोई स्मरण न रहेगा \q उनके बीच जो अंत में होंगे।
hi.B: जो पहले हो गए, उन्हें कोई याद नहीं करता, \q और जो अभी आनेवाले हैं, \q उन्हें भी वे याद नहीं करेंगे जो उनके बाद आएँगे।
hi.R: बहुत पहले जो लोग जीते थे, उन्हें कोई याद नहीं करता। \q और जो लोग अभी आनेवाले हैं, उन्हें भी उनके बाद जीनेवाले भूल जाएँगे।

ru.L: Нет воспоминания о прежних; \q и о поздних, которые будут, не будет о них воспоминания \q у тех, кто будет в последнее [время].
ru.B: Никто не помнит тех, кто жил раньше, \q и тех, кто ещё придёт, \q не вспомнят те, кто придёт после них.
ru.R: Никто не помнит людей, живших давным-давно. \q И тех, кто ещё будет жить, забудут те, кто будет жить после них.

ja.L: 先の[人々]の記憶はない。 \q また、これから現れる後の[人々]についても、彼らの記憶はない、 \q 終わりの時に現れる者たちのもとでは。
ja.B: 昔の人々を覚えている者はいない。 \q これから来る人々も、 \q その後に来る人々に覚えられることはない。
ja.R: 昔に生きた人々を、だれも覚えていない。 \q これから生まれて来る人々も、その後に生きる人々に忘れられてしまう。

uk.L: Немає памʼяті про колишніх; \q і також про пізніших, які будуть, не буде памʼяті про них \q у тих, хто буде після.
uk.B: Ніхто не памʼятає тих, хто був раніше, \q і тих, хто ще прийде, \q не памʼятатимуть ті, хто прийде після них.
uk.R: Ніхто не памʼятає людей, які жили давно. \q І тих, хто ще прийде, забудуть ті, хто житиме після них.

decisions.choice: the former ... the later: people of earlier and later times
alternatives: former and later things or events
decisions.reason: The words are masculine plurals and can mean earlier and later people or earlier and later things. After the generations of verse 4 they most likely mean people, though the claim holds of events too.

decisions.choice: no remembrance: being remembered is no lasting gain either
decisions.reason: To be remembered after death was a hope for a lasting name (Proverbs 10:7). Qoheleth says it fails too, for the wise and the fool alike (2:16; 9:5). The poem that began with generations going and coming (verse 4) ends with them forgotten.

decisions.choice: No one remembers ... will not be remembered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the Hebrew nouns into verbs, which English uses for this.

decisions.choice: Никто не помнит ... не вспомнят
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the Hebrew nouns into verbs, as Russian prefers here.

en.L: I, Qoheleth, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
en.B: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
en.R: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel. I ruled in Jerusalem.

es.B: Yo, el Maestro, fui rey de Israel en Jerusalén.
es.R: Yo, el Maestro, fui rey de Israel. Reiné en Jerusalén.

fr.L: Moi, Qohéleth, j’ai été roi sur Israël à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Moi, le Maître, j’ai été roi d’Israël à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Moi, le Maître, j’ai été roi d’Israël. J’ai régné à Jérusalem.
